newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bonds hold losses, ignore steady rates.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bonds hold losses, ignore steady rates.

text.p: Spanish government bonds fell on Tuesday, little affected by the Bank of Spain's decision to keep its key rate unchanged at 5.25 percent.
Although some traders said the peseta's strength might encourage a rate move, most analysts did not expect another reduction.
"The consensus was for rates to be unchanged," said Craig Shute, fixed-income analyst at Bear Stearns.
But scope for another rate cut continues to exist with inflation moderate and the peseta strong, although EMU worries could hurt the domestic scenario.
"The underlying domestic fundamentals are still supportive, but the sector is vulnerable to dilution from EMU worries," Shute said.
